question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+5z=5 \\ -x+5y-3z=2 \\ x-4y+7z=1\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & a & 5 \\ b & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -4 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+0y+5z=5 \\ -x+5y-3z=2 \\ x-4y+7z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ -1 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ -1 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -4 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=0,\,b=-1,\,c=5.$
